title: 'Crypto King' faked kidnapping, created video for sympathy, defence says
summary: A lawyer defending one of so-called "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski’s alleged kidnappers says the kidnapping was a "farce" and that Pleterski created a video pretending to be kidnapped in order to gain…

blocks.text: Toronto·New

A lawyer defending one of so-called "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski’s alleged kidnappers says the kidnapping was a "farce" and that Pleterski created a video pretending to be kidnapped in order to gain sympathy from his investors, who were trying to recover funds from him.
Lawyer for alleged kidnapper says Aiden Pleterski faked video so his investors would see it, have sympathy
'Crypto King' faked kidnapping, defence says

A lawyer defending one of so-called "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski's alleged kidnappers says the kidnapping was a "farce" and that Pleterski created a video pretending to be kidnapped in order to gain sympathy from his investors.
Pleterski denied both assertions while being cross-examined Thursday during the Toronto trial for three of his alleged kidnappers in Ontario Superior Court.

The video, which was played for the jury earlier in the trial and was previously obtained by CBC News, shows a beaten Pleterski apologizing to his investors and explaining what happened to their money.
Defence lawyer Leora Shemesh suggested Pleterski made the video himself to go viral and be seen by his investors, who were trying to recover their lost funds through a bankruptcy proceeding.
"This is an apology that's going to your very angry investors, who were going to see you with two black eyes and take pity and sympathy with you," she said.

items: Secretly recorded videos of 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski meeting alleged kidnapper played at trial
'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies he was beaten, tortured during alleged kidnapping

blocks.text: Shemesh is representing Alfredo Paladino who is charged — alongside Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry — with kidnapping and extorting Pleterski.
Pleterski previously testified that he was beaten, tortured and thought he was going to die during the three-day ordeal in early December 2022.

From left, Alfredo Paladino, Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry are accused of kidnapping and extorting the so-called 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski in December 2022. (Evan Mitsui/CBC, atlanticmastoronto/Instagram)

The Crown is alleging Heywood was the "driving force" behind the kidnapping and lost money investing with Pleterski, while Paladino and Henry carried out the kidnapping. Paladino and Henry are also charged with firearm and assault offences. All three men have pleaded not guilty.

Pleterski, who turned 28 on Wednesday, was convicted of fraud last month in connection with more than $30 million he took from investors to trade on their behalf. Instead, he spent much of it on his lifestyle. He has yet to be sentenced.
Pleterski questioned about kidnapping video
Pleterski testified Thursday that his kidnappers recorded the video while he was being held in a basement and instructed him on what to say.
"They told me to take all the blame for absolutely everything," he said.

Shemesh went through the transcript of the video line-by-line and questioned Pleterski about why he was including specific personal details such as how he was charged with assaulting his girlfriend in Florida and the year he began investing with his own money.
"During a kidnapping you told them that?" Shemesh pointedly asked him.
Pleterski said he was instructed to explain his story from the beginning and a lot of information, including the incident involving his girlfriend, was public at the time.
Defence lawyer Leora Shemesh, seen at right in this courtroom sketch, is representing Alfredo Paladino, right, in the trial involving the alleged kidnapping of Pleterski. (Pam Davies/CBC)

He testified that some of what he said in the nearly 14-minute video was true, some information was false — he said he was forced to say it by his kidnappers — and some he just said himself without instruction.

In the video, Pleterski details assets he "dispersed" to his former landlord Sandeep Gupta before his bankruptcy proceeding began, including luxury vehicles and at least two Rolex watches and a Jacob & Co. watch that he testified he bought for more than $300,000.

items: Crypto King's alleged kidnappers’ trial hears call Aiden Pleterski made to landlord asking for $3M
'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski testifies about escape attempt during alleged kidnapping

blocks.text: Pleterski testified Gupta wasn't actually hiding assets. He said he only told the kidnappers that so he could be released to set up a meeting with Gupta in hopes he would realize Pleterski was in trouble and alert the police.
Pleterski testified that he sold the Jacob & Co. watch and said he believed he got cash for it, but didn't remember who he sold it to or when, nor how he received the cash.
"Sandeep Gupta had your cars, Sandeep Gupta had your jewelry and Sandeep Gupta was holding money for you," Shemesh said.
Gupta testified earlier in the trial and denied hiding any assets for Pleterski.
Pleterski partied at rapper Drake's home

Heywood's defence lawyer, Hussein Aly, finished his cross-examination of Pleterski Thursday afternoon after two days of continually accusing Pleterski of lying, both while running a fraudulent investment scheme and during his testimony in the kidnapping trial.

Pleterski testified that Heywood invested with him then began threatening him about getting his money back. Pleterski said he was afraid after receiving threats from many people, including Heywood, so he hired security.
Aly questioned Pleterski about why he would hire a security company that belonged to Heywood's friend if Pleterski was being threatened by Heywood.

Akil Heywood's lawyer Hussein Aly showed the jury this photo of a group including Akil Heywood wearing a hat standing next to rapper Drake and the security guard wearing a blue shirt. Champagnepapi is Drake's instagram handle. (Akil Heywood/Facebook)
The jury heard the company is owned by Drake's security guard and Aly showed them photos of Heywood, Drake and the security guard together.
"You saw these photos on Akil Heywood's Instagram," Aly said to Pleterski.
Pleterski responded that he doesn't remember seeing them.
Aly also questioned why Pleterski went to a party at Drake's house in the spring of 2022 if he knew that Heywood was friends with the rapper.

Pleterski said he didn't know Heywood was going to be there, but said Heywood asked him for his money while at Drake's house, and that the security guard noticed the conversation, approached them, then put his hand on Heywood's shoulder and said "not here."

items: 'Crypto King' or 'Lying King'? Aiden Pleterski says he was neither at alleged kidnappers' trial

blocks.text: Aly has suggested Pleterski made up Heywood's involvement in the alleged kidnapping because he was mad about Heywood and another investor forcing Pleterski into bankruptcy.
"I could ask you questions for 100 days," Aly said to Pleterski. "You're never going to admit that you're lying about Akil Heywood's involvement in what happened to you."
Cross examination of Pleterski is expected to continue tomorrow afternoon.
